core_obligations: Sheaf property (proof lines 672-694): flat pullback commutes with cohomology sheaves; fpqc descent of quasi-coherent sheaves gives the Cech kernel, so the rules in (1) and (2) are fppf sheaves.
Etale reduction (proof lines 694-709): bootstrap and locality lemmas reduce to B affine.

Module realization and the cut (proof lines 711-741): realize K by pseudo-coherent M^bullet over A; fibre-wise vanishing of H^{-1} plus the cut-in-two lemma give M^bullet = tau_{>=0} (perfect, tor amplitude [0, b]) plus tau_{<=-1}; in case (2) the negative part vanishes so K is perfect with tor amplitude [0, b]; replace K by tau_{>=0}K using the dual vanishing lemma.

K-flat computation (proof lines 744-768): take the bounded finite-free representative; the last cokernel M is flat hence finite locally free; the resulting complex M -> M^1 -> ... is K-flat, so the functor computes as the kernel of Gamma(T, g^*M-tilde) -> Gamma(T, g^*M^1-tilde).
Explicit presentation (proof lines 770-798): shrink B so M and M^1 are finite free; the functor is the zero locus of m linear equations, represented by Spec(A[x_1..x_n]/(sum a_ij x_i)).
proof_roadmap: Verify the fppf sheaf property (proof lines 672-694).
Reduce etale locally to B affine and translate K to modules (proof lines 694-741).
Cut the complex, replace K by its positive truncation (proof lines 726-741).
Exhibit the functor as the kernel of a linear map of free modules via the K-flat representative (proof lines 744-768).
Write the explicit affine scheme presentation (proof lines 770-798).
